*** Add File: /Users/dwahl/Scripts/pantoken/formats/inline-styles/README.md
+# @pantoken/inline-styles
+
+Inline CSS into HTML with pantoken styles. This package is useful for email, static HTML, and other
+outputs where the main declarations need to live on matching elements while pseudo-classes,
+media queries, and similar fallbacks can remain in a `<style>` element.
+
+## Install
+
+```sh
+npm i @pantoken/inline-styles
+```
+
+Also available as `pantoken/inline-styles`.
+
+## Usage
+
+Inline a stylesheet into an HTML fragment:
+
+```ts
+import { inlineHtml } from "@pantoken/inline-styles/html";
+
+const html = inlineHtml(
+  '<button class="action">Save</button>',
+  ".action { color: red; } .action:hover { color: blue; }",
+);
+```
+
+Inline a complete pantoken theme and component stylesheet:
+
+```ts
+import { inlinePantokenHtml } from "@pantoken/inline-styles/pantoken-html";
+
+const html = inlinePantokenHtml("<button class=\"instui-button\">Save</button>", {
+  theme: "canvas",
+  mode: "dark",
+  customColor: "#e62429",
+  extraCss: ".notice { font-weight: 700; }",
+});
+```
+
+Pantoken inlining resolves token references for the selected theme and color scheme, so the
+resulting declarations do not depend on CSS custom properties. `inlineHtml` preserves fallback
+rules by default; set `preserveFallbacks: false` to remove the retained `<style>` rules. Use
+`resolveCSSVariables` when CSS variables should be resolved from document declarations.
+
+## CLI
+
+The `pantoken-inline` command reads HTML from stdin and writes the result to stdout:
+
+```sh
+cat page.html | pantoken-inline --theme canvas --mode dark > page.inlined.html
+```
+
+Use `--input` and `--output` for files. Other options are `--css <file>`, `--theme
+<rebrand|canvas|canvasHighContrast>`, `--mode <light|dark>`, `--prefix <name>`, and
+`--custom-color <hex>`.
+
+## API
+
+- **`inlineHtml(html, css, options?): string`** (from `@pantoken/inline-styles/html`) — inline
+  matching CSS declarations into an HTML string.
+- **`InlineHtmlOptions`** — controls fallback preservation and CSS variable resolution.
+- **`inlinePantokenHtml(html, options?): string`** (from
+  `@pantoken/inline-styles/pantoken-html`) — inline resolved pantoken tokens, component styles,
+  and optional custom CSS.
+- **`PantokenHtmlOptions`** — selects the theme, mode, component prefix, color scale, custom color,
+  fallback behavior, and additional CSS.
+
+## Related
+
+- Pairs with `@pantoken/components` for the component stylesheet and `@pantoken/tokens` for the
+  source token themes.
+- Use `@pantoken/css` when a stylesheet with custom properties is preferable to inline declarations.
+
+## License
+
+MIT
*** Add File: /Users/dwahl/Scripts/pantoken/formats/scope/README.md
+# @pantoken/scope
+
+Run several pantoken themes and color schemes in one document. Scopes apply theme, scheme, and
+color settings to a subtree, inherit independently from ancestors, and can form hard boundaries for
+previews or embedded applications.
+
+The package is browser-only and node-free. It supplies the runtime half of pantoken's scoped CSS
+contract; load the corresponding token/component stylesheets separately.
+
+## Install
+
+```sh
+npm i @pantoken/scope
+```
+
+Also available as `pantoken/scope`.
+
+## Usage
+
+Create independent scopes on the same page:
+
+```ts
+import { createScope } from "@pantoken/scope";
+
+const app = createScope(document.querySelector("#app")!, {
+  theme: "rebrand",
+  scheme: "dark",
+});
+
+const preview = createScope(document.querySelector("#preview")!, {
+  instanceId: "preview",
+  theme: "canvas",
+  scheme: "light",
+  boundary: true,
+});
+
+preview.set({ theme: "canvasHighContrast" });
+preview.set({ scheme: null }); // inherit the nearest scheme again
+```
+
+Each scope writes `data-pantoken-theme`, `data-pantoken-scheme`, and `data-pantoken-color` to its
+element. Descendants resolve each field independently. `boundary: true` prevents ancestors outside
+the scope from affecting it. Call `destroy()` when the scope is no longer needed.
+
+For an embedded document, connect the child frame to a host scope:
+
+```ts
+// In the host document
+const detach = app.attachFrame(document.querySelector("iframe")!);
+
+// In the frame
+import { connectScope } from "@pantoken/scope";
+
+const disconnect = connectScope({ hostOrigin: "https://example.test" });
+```
+
+The host sends updates only to frames explicitly attached to that scope. Use `"*"` as
+`hostOrigin` only for an opaque-origin `srcdoc` frame.
+
+## API
+
+- **`createScope(element, options?): PantokenScope`** — create and register a live scope. Its
+  methods include `get`, `set`, `resolve`, `attachFrame`, `subscribe`, and `destroy`.
+- **`getScope(instanceId?): PantokenScope | undefined`** — retrieve the registered scope for an
+  instance in the current document.
+- **`connectScope(options?): () => void`** — receive scope updates in an embedded document.
+- **`resolveScope(element): ResolvedScope`** — resolve theme, scheme, color, and instance by walking
+  ancestors. Resolution stops at a boundary or shadow root.
+- **`resolveScheme(element): "light" | "dark"`** and **`resolveInstance(element): string`** —
+  resolve the effective scheme or owning instance.
+- **`observeScope(element, listener): () => void`** — watch for changes to the resolved scope,
+  including changes made by an ancestor.
+- **`ensureProperties(css, options?): boolean`** and **`hasProperties(id?, doc?): boolean`** —
+  inject and check document-global `@property` registrations once per identifier.
+- **`ScopeConfig`**, **`ResolvedScope`**, **`PantokenScope`**, **`CreateScopeOptions`**, and
+  **`ConnectScopeOptions`** — runtime configuration and scope types.
+
+## Related
+
+- Pair with `@pantoken/css` or `@pantoken/components` stylesheets that select the
+  `data-pantoken-*` attributes.
+- Use `@pantoken/inline-styles` for static HTML output instead of browser-side scoped theming.
+
+## License
+
+MIT
*** End Patch"}

## Findings

`@pantoken/email` already reuses `@pantoken/inline-styles`; no new integration is currently needed.

- [platforms/email/src/index.ts](platforms/email/src/index.ts) exports:
  - `light`

- [platforms/email/src/inline.ts](platforms/email/src/inline.ts) aliases:
  - `inlinePantokenHtml` as `inlineEmailHtml`

- [platforms/email/package.json](platforms/email/package.json) already depends on `@pantoken/inline-styles` and exports `./inline`.
- [platforms/email/vite.config.ts](platforms/email/vite.config.ts) packages both `index` and `inline`.
- Generated [platforms/email/dist/inline.mjs](platforms/email/dist/inline.mjs) confirms the published API.

### Current inlining path

[formats/inline-styles/src/pantoken-html.ts](formats/inline-styles/src/pantoken-html.ts):

1. Selects a theme and light/dark mode.
2. Resolves token references into concrete values.
3. Generates a `:root` token stylesheet.
4. Adds custom color rules and all `componentsCss(...)`.
5. Appends caller CSS.
6. Delegates to `inlineHtml(...)`.

[formats/inline-styles/src/inline-html.ts](formats/inline-styles/src/inline-html.ts) uses Juice, with fallback preservation enabled by default for generic calls. `inlinePantokenHtml` changes the default to `preserveFallbacks: false`, so email output normally contains only inline declarations.

### Tests

[platforms/email/tests/index.test.ts](platforms/email/tests/index.test.ts) covers:

- Concrete non-`var(...)` token values.
- Light-mode selection.
- Basic button inlining.

[formats/inline-styles/tests/inline-html.test.ts](formats/inline-styles/tests/inline-html.test.ts) covers:

- Matching declarations.
- Pseudo-class fallbacks.
- CSS variable resolution.
- HTML/style injection protection.
- `@scope` flattening.
- Theme/mode combinations.
- Custom colors.

Missing email-specific coverage includes custom email options, `extraCss`, fallback behavior, prefixing, and malformed/unsupported email markup.

## Compatibility Risks

- `inlineEmailHtml` is only an alias, not an email-specific sanitizer. It inherits the full `@pantoken/components` stylesheet, including flexbox, pseudo-classes, media queries, shadows, and interactive component rules that many email clients ignore.
- `preserveFallbacks: false` removes retained `<style>` rules but does not filter unsupported inline CSS properties.
- The inliner is Node-oriented and brings Juice, Cheerio, and PostCSS. It inherits the Node `>=22.18.0` requirement and is unsuitable for browser bundles.
- HTML is parsed and serialized by Cheerio, so table markup, attributes, doctypes, and quoting may be normalized.
- `emailTokens` exposes only light/dark concrete maps, while `inlineEmailHtml` also supports themes, prefixes, custom colors, and extra CSS.
- The email README documents only token maps. It does not document the shipped `@pantoken/email/inline` API.
- `@pantoken/pantoken/email` and `pantoken/email` expose the root token API only; they do not expose `inlineEmailHtml`. Direct consumers must use `@pantoken/email/inline`.

2. Update [platforms/email/README.md](platforms/email/README.md) with `@pantoken/email/inline`, an example, supported options, and an explicit caveat that this does not guarantee email-client layout compatibility.

5. Treat aggregate-package access as a separate decision: add an aggregate inline subpath only if `@pantoken/pantoken/email` or `pantoken/email` must expose the inliner.

## Plan: Email-Compatible Inlining

Refactor the packages into two layers:

- `@pantoken/inline-styles`: generic Juice/PostCSS HTML/CSS inlining.
- `@pantoken/email`: pantoken-aware, email-safe output with configurable filtering and client profiles.

**Decisions**

- Move `inlinePantokenHtml` out of `@pantoken/inline-styles`.
- Preserve `emailTokens`, `light`, `dark`, and `@pantoken/email/inline`.
- Use a configurable class-name allowlist for email-safe components.
- Strip interactive states, unsupported components, and fallback `<style>` rules by default.
- Support `generic`, `outlook`/MSO, `gmail`, and `webkit` profiles in one conditional document.
- Do not generate automatic VML/table layouts in this phase.
- Keep `pantoken generate inline` generic.
- Add `pantoken generate email -i <file> -o <file>`.

**Implementation**

1. Refactor `formats/inline-styles`
   - Retain generic `inlineHtml`.
   - Remove token/theme/component resolution and related dependencies.
   - Support embedded `<style>` blocks plus optional `--css`.
   - Update tests and README.

2. Expand `platforms/email`
   - Move token resolution into email-owned modules.
   - Add email HTML generation.
   - Add configurable component filtering and state/fallback removal.
   - Add client capability profiles and conditional output.
   - Preserve existing token-map APIs and `@pantoken/email/inline`.
   - Add focused filtering, profile, mode, custom-color, and output tests.

3. Update `packages/cli`
   - Keep `generate inline` generic.
   - Add `generate email` with client/profile options.
   - Update parser, help, dependencies, README, and end-to-end tests.

4. Regenerate aggregate packages and update:
   - `platforms/email/README.md`
   - `formats/inline-styles/README.md`
   - `packages/cli/README.md`
   - Security documentation if the input/serialization surface changes.
   - Patch changesets for affected packages.

**Verification**

- Focused generic inliner, email, and CLI tests.
- Package `vp check` for all three affected packages.
- Markdown lint and export/package validation.
- Manual inspection of representative HTML for generic, Outlook, Gmail, and WebKit profiles.

The detailed plan is saved in `/memories/session/plan.md` and is ready for implementation approval.
